A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GuideFlow work, and all 11 pages of each are readable and directly comparable. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, despite references to one; the comparison covers all supplied material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative trajectory comparisons in Sections 5–6, Tables 1–6, and Figure 4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative comparisons reported in v1.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same flow generator, classifier-free guidance, CVF, CF, RFE, reward conditioning, training objectives, and sampling procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same driving tasks and scenarios on NuScenes, ADV-NuScenes, NavSim/Navhard, and Bench2Drive. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within Tables 1–3 and Figure 4, including the same GTRS variants, DiffVLA, DriveSuprim, DiffusionDrive, and SparseDrive comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains identical splits, metrics, backbones, training budgets, and evaluation procedures, including 100 NavTrain epochs and evaluation on 220 Bench2Drive routes.

E4.justification: Tables 4–6 retain the same conditioning, constraint-module, reward-conditioning, and hyperparameter analyses. Figure 4 retains the same qualitative driving cases; no additional appendix analyses are supplied in either PDF.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–6 and the qualitative findings in Figure 4 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains 43.0 EPDMS for GuideFlow + Scorer, and Table 2 retains 75.21 Driving Score and 51.36% Success Rate.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, energy-matching derivation, and Equations (1)–(18) are unchanged. The appendix proof referenced in Section 4.3 is absent from both supplied PDFs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about multimodal planning, explicit constraint enforcement, EBM integration, controllable aggressiveness, and benchmark performance, including the 43.0 EPDMS SOTA claim.

C2.justification: The explanations of module effectiveness, the tradeoff between aggressiveness and safety, and the limitation that accelerated sampling can reduce performance are unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the generic promise of a code release to a promise naming the liulin815/GuideFlow GitHub repository. This adds resource-location information but does not establish that code has been released; implementation details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the positioning against earlier planners, and all 48 references are unchanged. The repository pointer is not an addition to related research.

P1.justification: The displayed author name changes from 'Yandan Luo' to 'Yadan Luo', Figure 3's caption loses a stray 'ß', and the code-release sentence gains a repository address. The scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added repository address causes limited first-page reflow, and Figure 3's caption is corrected. The figures themselves, table structures, and remaining page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Removing the stray caption character and specifying the planned code-release location modestly improve presentation and resource discoverability. The benefit is limited: neither actual code availability nor any improvement to the scientific evidence is established, and the referenced appendices remain absent.
